title: Prospective randomized trial of hypofractionated proton therapy compared to hypofractionated IMRT in prostate tumors
summary:
Many men with prostate cancer are treated with radiation therapy. In order to shorten the duration of treatment, hypofractionated radiation therapy is increasingly being used, which requires fewer sessions with higher radiation doses. However, this therapy can cause side effects, particularly in the urinary and gastrointestinal tract.
Proton therapy is a special form of radiation therapy that treats the tumor in a very targeted manner and is gentler on the surrounding healthy tissue. This could result in fewer side effects than with conventional photon therapy. Initial summaries of earlier studies suggest that this may be the case, but there are currently no meaningful direct comparative studies.
The aim of this study is therefore to investigate whether hypofractionated proton therapy causes fewer side effects in patients with prostate cancer compared to hypofractionated photon therapy, is equally effective, and improves the quality of life of patients.
To this end, patients are randomly assigned (randomization) to one of the two study arms. Patients in study arm A receive hypofractionated radiation therapy with photons. Patients in study arm B receive hypofractionated radiation therapy with protons.

interventions.name: Hypofractionated photon radiation therapy with a total dose of 62 Gy in 20 fractions (3.1 Gy single dose) over approx. 4 weeks.
Hypofractionated proton beam therapy with a total dose of 62 Gy (RBE) in 20 fractions (3.1 Gy (RBE) single dose) over approx. 4 weeks

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Histologically confirmed diagnosis of prostate adenocarcinoma
- Clinical stage T1-T3
- Gleason score ≤ 8
- Indication for hypofractionated radiotherapy with a total radiation dose of 62 Gy (RBE).
- ECOG performance status 0-2
- Age ≥ 18 years
- Ability to give informed consent
- Willingness to complete questionnaires on quality of life and to attend regular study visits
- Availability of a written declaration of consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Previous radiation or chemotherapy of the pelvis for prostate tumors.
- Concurrent radiation therapy of the pelvis
- Previous prostate tumor treatments such as prostatectomy or cryotherapy.
- Concurrent cytotoxic chemotherapy
- Evidence of lymph node involvement or distant metastases
- Presence of a hip prosthesis or other conditions that could interfere with imaging.
- Severe urinary symptoms (IPSS > 20)
- Concurrent participation in another clinical trial that conflicts with this trial
- Incapable of giving consent
